text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where contributing to the group multiplies value but mostly benefits others, so keeping tokens is individually dominant even though full contribution is socially optimal. I'm leaning toward a moderate cooperative contribution rather than going fully selfish or fully altruistic.

Given the personal loss from contributing versus potential returns from others' contributions, I'll just pick 10 as a simple, cooperative signal to start.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where contributing tokens benefits the group more than the individual, since each token contributed returns only 0.3 to the contributor but 1.2 split across the group, while keeping it yields the full 1 to self. The dominant individual strategy is to contribute nothing, yet full cooperation maximizes collective payoff over the 10 rounds—so I'm weighing a moderate starting contribution as a reasonable approach.
